{"id": "f0c264eb-1801-437d-b0d4-33b9da2fa3f0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Yes, it grows without limit, but the cost is tiny at your current volume.**

**What I found (account 012345678901_1, us-east-1):**
- Bedrock invocation logging writes to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There is no S3 destination.
- **The log group has no retention policy set.** Logs are never expired, so storage only goes up.
- The log group was created around Oct 15, 2026. It now holds about 124 MB (about 0.12 GB) in the Standard class, so roughly 3 MB per day.

**What that costs:**
- At about $0.03 per GB-month (approximate us-east-1 Standard pricing, which I haven't checked against the current price list), 124 MB is well under a cent per month.
- At the current rate you'd add about 1 GB per year, or about $0.03 per month more each year. Storage is not a concern at this volume.
- Ingestion is the larger cost, at about $0.50 per GB. That is a one-time charge as logs arrive, and it scales with your Bedrock traffic, not with how long you keep the logs.

**Things to watch:**
- If your Bedrock usage rises sharply, the 3 MB per day figure will rise with it, and unbounded retention will matter more.
- Text and video data delivery are both enabled. Prompts and responses in these logs can contain sensitive data. If you have data-retention requirements, an indefinite retention period may also be a compliance issue.
- The configuration has no S3 destination. Bedrock sends large payloads to S3 when one is configured, so very large inputs and outputs may not be captured in full here.

I can set a retention period on the log group, such as 30, 90 or 365 days. The change needs your approval, and logs older than the period would then expire. Tell me which period you want.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
